name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican House seats in the country
Incumbent Riley Moore holds a roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage over Ace Parsi
Prediction markets price a Moore win at about 97 percent
No public general-election polling; the challenger remains lightly funded
model.rationale: The district's twenty-point Republican lean, Moore's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and market pricing near 97 percent all point the same direction, and no polling or ratings evidence suggests the challenger can close a gap of this size.
model.watch: A dramatic national wave toward Democrats or an unexpected scandal involving Moore could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
WV-02 is one of the most Republican-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty points toward the GOP. Incumbent Riley Moore is running for re-election and has raised about $1.6 million, holding a large financial edge over Democratic challenger Ace Parsi, who has brought in roughly $277,000. No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters currently list the race, but prediction markets give Moore about a 97 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point firmly toward a Republican hold. The challenger would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or an unexpected development in the district to close a gap this wide. As it stands, the race is rated Safe Republican, with Moore expected to win by a comfortable double-digit margin.
